subject: Clarify regional uptime floor & monthly credit mechanic — proposal
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha@monterey-analytics.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@monterey-analytics.com
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SLA questions for Redwood pilot

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re excited to pilot Redwood for our query-ranking workloads. Before we sign the pilot SOW, procurement asked for some clarifications on the SLA template you sent over: specifically how the monthly credit mechanics interact with regional uptime floors. A couple of direct questions:

- If we have a cross-region deployment (US primary, EU standby) and the US region meets 99.9% but EU dips to 99.5% in a given month, how is the remedy calculated?
- Is there a per-region credit cap per month, or a single account-wide cap?
- Can we request a temporary latency carveout during the onboarding month when we’ll be doing heavy cache warm-up?

I attached the SLA draft with inline comments (see attachment stub). Can you confirm whether Redwood would accept a regional carveout during onboarding, and how monthly credits would be computed if only a single region breaches?

Appreciate it — if it’s easier we can hop on a quick call Monday.

Best,
Samantha Cho
Head of Cloud Ops
Monterey Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated draft. I pulled together a short summary below and attached an updated SLA snippet + a spreadsheet that shows the math for a regional vs account-wide approach. High level answers:

- Regional breaches are assessed per-region, and remedies are calculated against that region’s monthly usage. In practice that means if EU falls below the uptime floor we calculate credits using the EU token/usage for that month.
- We support either a per-region cap or an account-wide cap — for pilots we’ve generally accepted account-wide caps to keep billing predictable. Our standard account-wide cap is 25% of the region’s monthly bill, but we can discuss a lower pilot cap.
- We can agree a one-month onboarding latency carveout if it’s limited in scope (eg: excluded P95 latency breaches for non-production prefixes, and a clear start/end date). We’d need that in the SOW.

Notes attached: Redwood-SLA-draft-v2.pdf (redlines) and monthly-credit-calculation.xlsx (worked examples).

Quick ask: Lauren (cc’d) handles regional legal and ops — looping her in to confirm the onboarding carveout language and whether we can reduce the credit cap for a pilot.

If you’re free Monday at 11am PT I can have Lauren join as well.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Ben / Samantha — quick follow-up from our side after reviewing the spreadsheet. Two operational points to consider when you (Monterey) decide between per-region vs account-wide caps:

1) Billing alignment: if you expect EU usage to be <15% of total tokens in early months, an account-wide cap at 25% could over-index the remedy against total spend and result in unexpectedly high credits for a small region. For pilots we often set a reduced account cap (eg. max 10% of total monthly) OR keep per-region caps with a soft escalator if usage shifts.

2) Latency carveout: we will accept a one-month onboarding carveout for p95 latency on non-production prefixes, but we need a short mutual action plan (MAP) in the SOW listing what metrics we’ll collect, who will own cache-warm actions, and an agreed end date. If Monterey wants the carveout to include production traffic we’d need a narrower scope and a temporary elevated support tier for the month (paid).

I’ve drafted a MAP blurb in the attached SLA snippet (see Redwood-SLA-draft-v2.pdf page 2) — please review.

—Rishi
